**3B.7 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Working judgment:** `Partial / limited yes`. Marcos’s government did take some real steps that helped vulnerable groups, especially through disaster response, aid delivery, and the POGO ban. But the broader record still shows red-tagging, threats against activists and journalists, and no clear system-wide protection for minorities or other vulnerable groups from politically tolerated intimidation.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | SWS survey: PBBM very good on helping disaster victims, improving children’s quality of education, helping the poor | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-14 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/sws-survey-pbbm-very-good-on-helping-disaster-victims-improving-childrens-quality-of-education-helping-the-poor/ | The administration highlighted strong survey results on disaster response, education, and aid to the poor. This is the clearest evidence of active protection for vulnerable groups through service delivery. | 3B.7, 2B.10 |
| Positive | Gov’t vows legal action vs deep fake video creators, spreaders | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | The government said DICT and the NSC were investigating a deepfake and considering legal action. This helped protect the public, including vulnerable groups, from manipulative disinformation. | 3B.7, 3B.6, 3B.5 |
| Positive | PCO to designate fact-check officers in state media to fight fake news | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-09 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/ | PCO said it would place fact-check officers in state media and denied a policy of red-tagging. This is modest but real evidence of a protective information environment. | 3B.7, 3B.6, 3B.3 |
| Positive | DOJ creates task force to review EJK cases | Philippine News Agency | 2024-11-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266 | The DOJ created a task force to investigate extrajudicial killings and file charges if warranted. That matters for vulnerable groups because it signals some willingness to protect them from abuse and impunity. | 3B.7, 3B.4, 3B.1 |
| Positive | Marcos bans POGOs, cites disorder it caused PH | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964063/marcos-bans-pogo-cites-disorder-it-caused-ph | Marcos banned POGOs after citing torture, kidnapping, trafficking, and murder associated with the sector. This is concrete protection against a network that harmed women, migrants, and other vulnerable people. | 3B.7, 3B.4, 3B.2 |
| Positive | Marcos announces ban on all POGO | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914272/marcos-announces-ban-on-all-pogo/story/ | The ban was framed as stopping “grave abuse” and illegal acts and winding the industry down. This supports a limited claim that Marcos sometimes acted to protect vulnerable people from exploitation. | 3B.7, 3B.4, 3B.2 |
| Negative | World Report 2024: Philippines | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/philippines | HRW says red-tagging by authorities and supporters continued and often exposed activists, unionists, Indigenous leaders, students, and journalists to danger. This undercuts any claim of broad protection for minorities or vulnerable groups. | 3B.7, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines: “I turned my fear into courage”: Red-tagging and state violence against young human rights defenders in the Philippines | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | Amnesty says Marcos-era actors used misinformation and anti-terror framing to create fear, and red-tagging vilified activists, journalists, teachers, and others as terrorists or communists. This is direct evidence against a clean protection record. | 3B.7, 3B.6, 3B.3 |
| Negative | Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reports officials and police or military members threatened union leaders by linking them to communism. That is targeted intimidation rather than protection of vulnerable workers. | 3B.7, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | The report notes red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos. This shows a continuing coercive climate around vulnerable civic groups. | 3B.7, 3B.3, 3B.6 |
| Negative | 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | The report lists credible abuses including killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, and police/security-force abuse. It also indicates vulnerable people remained exposed despite some policy reform. | 3B.7, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines: “Submit and surrender”: the harms of arbitrary drug detention in the Philippines | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8759/2024/en/ | Amnesty documents torture, ill-treatment, arbitrary detention, and coerced confessions in drug centers. This is especially relevant for marginalized users of the drug system, including poor and vulnerable families. | 3B.7, 3B.1, 3B.2 |

**Synthesis**
- Marcos did take some real protective actions for vulnerable groups, especially through disaster response, education, social aid, anti-deepfake response, and the POGO ban.
- Those are meaningful, but they do not amount to a comprehensive protection regime.
- The negative record remains strong: red-tagging, threats against activists, journalists, labor leaders, and Indigenous leaders, plus continuing abuse in drug-related custody settings.
- Best overall read: `some protective governance, but persistent vulnerability and intimidation`.

**Search gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a dedicated, president-led protection program specifically for women, children, Indigenous peoples, minorities, or displaced communities that clearly reversed the underlying risk environment.
- The positive evidence is mostly indirect, sectoral, or service-delivery based rather than a direct answer to targeted violence against protected groups.
